nodes.name: NotificationsHandler

nodes.name: recipe.ts

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand Ferdium at a high level: a hard-fork of Franz that aggregates messaging services (WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, etc.) into a single Electron desktop app. This document outlines the project's purpose, download links, migration guides from Ferdi, custom styling support, and contribution workflow, providing essential context before diving into the codebase.

tour.title: Electron Main Process Entry
tour.description: The main process entry point (`src/index.ts`) bootstraps the entire application: it initializes Electron window management, deep linking, auto-updates, the tray icon, and IPC handlers. Its sibling `electron-util.ts` provides platform-agnostic Electron utilities. This is where the app's runtime lifecycle begins — understanding this file reveals how all the pieces (settings, error handling, menus, IPC) get wired together at startup.
tour.languageLesson: Electron has two process types: the main process (Node.js, manages windows/system) and renderer processes (Chromium, runs the UI). IPC bridges them via contextBridge and ipcRenderer/ipcMain.

tour.title: Core Configuration and Platform
tour.description: Two files form the foundation that nearly every other module depends on. `src/config.ts` is the most imported file in the entire codebase (fan-in: 56), providing shared constants and build-time settings. `src/environment.ts` detects the OS platform (Mac, Windows, Linux, Snap) and defines keyboard shortcut keys used throughout the app. These are the first modules loaded after startup — everything builds on top of them.

tour.title: React Renderer and Navigation
tour.description: The React side of the app starts at `src/app.tsx`, which initializes both API backends (server and local), creates the MobX stores, mounts the React tree with routing, and sets up the Menu/TouchBar factories. `src/routes.tsx` defines the full React Router v6 navigation tree — authentication screens, settings, service views, and feature pages. This is the highest fan-out file (29 edges), making it the best map of the application's screen structure.
tour.languageLesson: React 18's createRoot API replaces ReactDOM.render. Combined with React Router v6's nested route layout, it enables co-located data loading and error boundaries per route segment.

tour.title: MobX State Management Layer
tour.description: Ferdium uses MobX for reactive state management across the entire application. The stores barrel (`src/stores/index.ts`) defines the `RealStores` interface listing every store type — AppStore, ServicesStore, SettingsStore, UIStore, UserStore, and more — and wires them together with shared dependencies. The actions barrel (`src/actions/index.ts`) aggregates all action dispatchers, including feature actions for workspaces and todos. This layer is the brain of the application: stores hold state, actions mutate it.
tour.languageLesson: MobX uses observable decorators to make class properties reactive. Actions batch mutations, and computed values derive state automatically. Stores are singletons injected via React context, enabling any component to access any store.

tour.title: API and Backend Communication
tour.description: The API layer (`src/api/index.ts`) creates a factory that instantiates typed API classes for every domain — services, recipes, users, features, app health — routing requests to either the remote Ferdium server or the embedded local server. `src/api/apiBase.ts` handles URL resolution, auth token management for the local server, and server type identification (Franz/Ferdium/Local/Custom). This dual-backend architecture enables both online (Ferdium account) and offline (local-first) usage seamlessly.

tour.title: Service and Recipe Integration System
tour.description: At Ferdium's heart is the recipe system: `src/models/Recipe.ts` defines a service template (URL pattern, message capabilities, dark mode support), while `src/models/Service.ts` represents a running instance with its own WebView, partition isolation, and observable state (unread counts, enabled/muted flags). The recipe WebView controller (`src/webview/recipe.ts`) orchestrates the full service lifecycle in the renderer — badge handling, dark mode injection, dialog title management, find-in-page, spell checking, and screen sharing — all via a unified RecipeController class. This is the most fan-out-heavy file in the webview layer (18 outgoing edges).
tour.languageLesson: Electron's WebView tag renders web content in isolation with its own session partition. This is how Ferdium loads WhatsApp, Slack, etc. without cross-contamination — each service gets a unique partition for cookies, storage, and cache.

tour.title: Core Business Logic Stores
tour.description: The two most important stores drive the application's primary functionality. `ServicesStore` manages the full service lifecycle: CRUD operations, reordering, unread count aggregation, mute/snooze toggling, and split-mode visibility. `AppStore` tracks global state — online/offline connectivity, update availability, locale, fullscreen status, and the app locking mechanism. Together they form the bridge between the UI layer (Step 4) and the data model (Step 7), reacting to user actions and API responses.

tour.title: Local Server and Containerization
tour.description: Ferdium embeds an AdonisJS 5 server (`src/internal-server/start.ts`) with its own SQLite database, controllers, migrations, and routes — enabling full offline/local-first operation without requiring a Ferdium account. Matching this, the Dockerfile (`service:Dockerfile`) uses a multi-stage build: the builder stage compiles TypeScript and builds recipes in a full Node.js environment, while the final stage copies only runtime artifacts into a minimal busybox image. Two approaches to deployment — one for development flexibility, one for production packaging.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use separate FROM statements for build-time (full SDK) and run-time (minimal base). This keeps the production image small while retaining everything needed to execute the compiled app.

tour.title: UI Shell and Theming System
tour.description: The main application shell (`src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx`) renders the complete UI layout: sidebar with service tabs, workspaces drawer, services viewport, todos panel, info bars, and overlays for auth, basic auth, and quick switch. The theme system (`concept:theme-system`) supports three themes (default, dark, legacy) defined in `src/themes/`, while the SCSS style system (`concept:scss-style-system`, fan-in: 25) provides a flat modular collection of 30+ style files covering layout, colors, typography, animations, and component-specific styles. This is where the user-facing experience comes together.

tour.title: CI/CD and Build Configuration
tour.description: The CI/CD pipeline (`builds.yml`) builds Ferdium for macOS, Linux, and Windows with code signing, notarization, Snap publishing, and GitHub Releases deployment — triggered on develop, nightly, and release branches. The root `package.json` defines the project metadata (version 7.1.3-nightly.3), scripts for dev/build/test/lint, and dependencies spanning React 18, MobX 6, MUI 5, AdonisJS 5, and Electron. This infrastructure stop reveals how the code you've explored gets tested, packaged, and distributed to users across all platforms.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrix builds parallelize across OS targets. Each job runs in an isolated runner with cached dependencies, making CI fast and reproducible. The release workflow tags, packages, and uploads platform-specific artifacts in a single pipeline.
